text:
sara: FYI ticket #3452 from Acme — their A/B rollout dashboard shows assignments flipped (control/variant swapped) and counts off by ~2x. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/exp_acme_home_cta_v2 -> screenshot attached

matt: @sara can you paste the experiment key + a couple sample user ids? saw similar when keys were reused across imports

sara: exp key: exp_acme_home_cta_v2. sample user_ids: 12345, 67890, 55555. csv attached to ticket. customer says users that should be in control are showing in variant in dashboard view

analytics-bot: anomaly alert — cohort assignment delta >150% for exp_acme_home_cta_v2 between 2026-03-16T00:00Z and 2026-03-16T04:00Z

julia: pulled raw assignment counts from the assignments table:
```
SELECT variant_key, count(*) FROM assignments
WHERE experiment_key='exp_acme_home_cta_v2' AND ts >= '2026-03-15' GROUP BY variant_key;
-- result: variant_a: 3,200  control: 12,100
```
This is inverse of what the rollout config shows (expected control ~3k). attaching query CSV

devon: I repro'd locally with a small trace. Dashboard does a join: assignments -> rollouts_metadata by numeric experiment_id, while the UI label mapping pulls experiment.display_name from experiments table. If two experiment_keys got mapped to same numeric id (migration/import), labels can get attached to the wrong assignment rows

matt: can you dump the assignments rows for user 12345?

julia: row for user 12345: `user_id=12345, experiment_key=exp_acme_home_cta_v2, variant_key=control, hashed_bucket=0.12, assigned_at=2026-03-16T01:12:34Z` — backend assignment shows control, but dashboard UI shows variant_a for that user

ingrid: looking at rollouts_metadata table — during last week's metadata migration a script collapsed keys by stripping suffixes. Two entries now share numeric_id=9012: `exp_acme_home_cta` and `exp_acme_home_cta_v2`. frontend code uses numeric_id for mapping in some places, which explains swapped labels

devon: quick mitigation: change API mapping to prefer full experiment_key when present. Patch idea below — minimal and hotpatchable: 
```
# before
mapping = get_experiment_by_id(experiment.numeric_id)
# after
mapping = get_experiment_by_key(experiment.full_key) or get_experiment_by_id(experiment.numeric_id)
```
This avoids relying solely on numeric id for label resolution. Will add a guard to log mismatches for >0.1% of requests

matt: can we do a staged hotpatch? push to staging, smoke-test with sample ids, then rollout to prod. If mapping fix is safe we can also run a data-repair job to backfill dashboard summaries. ETA ~2-3h

sara: told customer ETA 3h, they accepted temporary notice on dashboard saying "counts under investigation" :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy started by matt — deploy-4872 to prod

matt: hotpatch deployed to staging, smoke tests OK. deploying to prod now

ops-bot: deploy succeeded — deploy-4872 completed (prod)

matt: kicked off data-repair job to recompute rollout aggregates for the past 72h (job id: repair-774). logs: `repair-774: scanned 1.1M assignment rows, corrected label mapping for 4,200 rows`

julia: re-queried dashboard join after repair, counts now match assignments table for sample ids (12345 shows control in UI). Verified A/B split aligns with rollout config.

support-bot: ticket #3452 status -> escalated -> resolved (pending 24h monitoring)

sara: thanks all. follow-ups: add uniqueness constraint on experiments.key, add migration safety checks (don't strip suffixes), add integration test for mapping logic. I'll log RFC and follow-up tasks in #eng-infra

matt: logging follow-up PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/542 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/789 — assign to ingrid/devon for migration tests

julia: monitoring alert re: assignment-delta cleared. will leave ticket pending for 24h then close

sara: resolved -> closing after 24h. thanks :rocket:
